statutes.text_quote: DOES NOT EXIST. Title 40, Chapter 7 ("Off-Road Vehicle Act of 1975") runs §§ 40-7-1 to 40-7-6 only; Justia 2025 chapter index shows "Chapter 7 - Off-Road Vehicles (§§ 40-7-1 — 40-7-6)".

statutes.text_quote: "off-road vehicle" means any motorized vehicle designed for or capable of cross-country travel ... and not intended for use predominantly on public roads.

violation to operate an off-road vehicle "(1) Without operative brakes or without mufflers ...; (2) On any private property without the express written permission of the owner ...; or (3) Within any perennial stream, except when directly crossing such stream."
"Incorporated towns and municipalities and counties shall have the authority to adopt ordinances ... to regulate time periods and zones of use for off-road vehicles."
statutes.verified_how: OCGA mirror (2021 release); listed unchanged in Justia 2025 chapter index.

statutes.text_quote: violator "shall not thereby be guilty of a criminal act but shall be subject to a civil penalty of not less than $25.00."
statutes.verified_how: OCGA mirror (2021 release); listed in Justia 2025 index.

statutes.text_quote: "(b) A farmer who is 16 years of age or older may operate a farm use vehicle on any public road or highway of this state so long as: (1) ... emblem conforming to ... Code Section 40-8-4; and (2) ... actively being operated by such farmer to transport: (A) Agricultural products, livestock, farm machinery, or farm supplies to or from a farm; or (B) Such farmer between his or her residence and the farm..." "Farm use vehicle" means an all-terrain vehicle or personal transportation vehicle.
farm use vehicle operator "shall be granted all of the rights and shall be subject to all of the duties applicable to the driver of any other vehicle".
statutes.verified_how: OCGA mirror (2021 release) only; Part 1B page not opened. URL given is the adjacent § 40-6-305 page (same Part, has a Next link to § 40-6-306).

statutes.text_quote: (3) "All-terrain vehicle" means a motorized vehicle originally manufactured for off-highway use which is equipped with three or more nonhighway tires, is 80 inches or less in width with a dry weight of 3,500 pounds or less...; (33.1) "Multipurpose off-highway vehicle" ... uses a steering wheel ... nonstraddle seat.

statutes.cite: S.C. Code § 50-26-10 to -70 (Chandler's Law, 2011 Act No. 24)
statutes.text_quote: § 50-26-30: (A) unlawful for parent to knowingly permit under-6 to operate an ATV; (B) under-16 unlicensed may not carry a passenger; (F) 15 and younger must possess a hands-on ATV safety course certificate; (G) 15 and younger must wear FMVSS 218 helmet and eye protection. § 50-26-40 (lands open to the public): (C) 16 and younger must be accompanied by an adult; headlights at night; no reckless/DUI. § 50-26-60 misdemeanor $50-$200. § 50-26-70 exceptions: farming/ranching, hunting/trapping, ages 6-15 on private property under direct parental visual supervision. § 50-26-20 ATV = handlebars, three or more wheels (UTVs with steering wheels excluded).
"Every motor vehicle ... driven, operated or moved upon a highway in this State shall be registered and licensed ... It shall be a misdemeanor" to operate one that is not.
"Off Road Use Only" brand designates a vehicle "not manufactured for use on public roads. The department shall not register and license the vehicle pursuant to Section 56-3-350."
statutes.verified_how: scstatehouse.gov fetched 2026-10-05 (current text; amended by Act 164 eff. 11/18/2026 to add "unless otherwise specified in Article 5").

statutes.text_quote: Signed 5/18/2026, effective 11/18/2026. UTV = side-by-side, steering wheel, nonstraddle seat, top speed over 55 mph, ≥450cc, ≤80 in wide. Operator 17+ with full license, plate, registration, insurance (§ 56-2-5010); no interstates (§ 56-2-5080); absent local ordinance, only secondary highways ≤55 mph within 10 miles of registered address (§ 56-2-5110); under-21 helmet/eye protection, seat belts, no passengers under 8; farmers with SCATE card may operate within 10 miles of the farm (§ 56-2-5140).
statutes.verified_how: scstatehouse.gov bill page fetched 2026-10-05 (enrolled text; codified section numbers as stated in the act).

replacements.old_sentence_exact: O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120 et seq. restricts ATV use on public roads to specific circumstances (agricultural use, certain crossings).
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia does not generally allow ATVs on public roads; O.C.G.A. § 40-6-305 lets farmers 16 and older use one for farm hauling.
replacements.note: PRIMARY. § 40-7-120 does not exist; Chapter 7 ends at § 40-7-6. Agricultural exception is real (§ 40-6-305) but no Georgia statute creates a road-crossing exception — dropped. Old link points to a nonexistent Justia "article-5".

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Children under 16 may not operate ATVs on public property without supervision.
replacements.new_sentence: O.C.G.A. § 40-7-4 requires off-road vehicles to have working brakes and mufflers.
replacements.note: ADJACENT unsupported claim: Georgia has no statutory ATV age or supervision rule. Replaced with what § 40-7-4 actually requires (also bars riding on private land without the owner's written permission). Alternatively delete.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: ATVs are not street-legal in Georgia without specific modifications and registration.
replacements.note: ADJACENT: implies modification + registration makes an ATV road-legal; no Georgia statute provides that. Recommend deleting (new_sentence empty).

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Georgia law (O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120 et seq.) restricts ATV operation on public roads to limited circumstances, such as agricultural use and supervised road crossings.
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia law does not generally authorize it; the main exception (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-305) lets farmers 16 and older use an ATV on public roads for farm transport.
replacements.note: PRIMARY. Keep the preceding "Generally no." No supervised-crossing exception exists in Georgia statute.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: ATVs are not street-legal without specific modifications.
replacements.new_sentence: ATVs are built for off-highway use (O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(3)).
replacements.note: ADJACENT: same unsupported "modifications" implication; replaced with the statutory definition.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Georgia regulates ATV operation under O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120 et seq., which establishes requirements for ATV use on public and private land, age restrictions for operators, and safety equipment mandates.
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia regulates ATVs as off-road vehicles under O.C.G.A. § 40-7-1 et seq., which requires working brakes and a muffler and bars riding on private land without the owner's written permission.
replacements.note: PRIMARY. Chapter 7 (§§ 40-7-1 to -6) has no age restrictions or safety-gear mandates; its equipment rule is brakes + muffler (§ 40-7-4(1)).

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Georgia law prohibits operating an ATV on public roads (with limited exceptions for agricultural and crossing purposes) and requires riders under 16 to complete an approved safety course.
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia law does not generally authorize ATVs on public roads; O.C.G.A. § 40-6-305 allows farmers 16 and older to use them there for farm transport.
replacements.note: ADJACENT. No crossing exception and NO Georgia safety-course requirement for under-16 riders exist in statute (that rule is South Carolina's, § 50-26-30(F), for 15 and younger).

replacements.old_sentence_exact: South Carolina regulates ATV use under S.C. Code § 56-15-10 et seq. and local ordinances.
replacements.new_sentence: South Carolina regulates ATV use under S.C. Code § 50-26-10 et seq. and local ordinances.
replacements.note: SC cite fix. § 56-15-10 is the definitions section of the motor vehicle manufacturers/distributors/dealers chapter. The following sentence (road restriction + supervision for minors) is supportable: § 56-1-10(37)/§ 56-3-110 and § 50-26-40(C).

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Georgia law under O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120 et seq. classifies side-by-side vehicles alongside ATVs for regulatory purposes, restricting their use on public roads and establishing age and safety requirements.
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia treats side-by-sides, like ATVs, as off-road vehicles under O.C.G.A. § 40-7-1 et seq., and its law does not generally authorize them on public roads.
replacements.note: PRIMARY. § 40-7-3 "off-road vehicle" covers both; § 40-1-1 defines ATV (3) and "multipurpose off-highway vehicle" (33.1, steering wheel, nonstraddle seat) separately. No Georgia age/safety rules for UTVs. Note the § 40-6-305 farm exception covers ATVs and PTVs only, not MOHVs.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: South Carolina regulates off-highway vehicles under S.C. Code § 56-15-10 et seq., with similar restrictions on road use and requirements for equipment standards.
replacements.new_sentence: South Carolina bars unregistered off-road vehicles from highways (S.C. Code § 56-3-110); registered UTVs may use some roads from Nov. 18, 2026 (Act 164).

cites.cite: 2026 S.C. Act No. 164 (S. 222), adding S.C. Code §§ 56-2-5000 et seq., eff. Nov. 18, 2026

replacements.note: TIME-SENSITIVE: 2026 S.C. Act No. 164 (S. 222, signed 5/18/2026) takes effect 11/18/2026 — registered UTVs (17+, licensed, insured, belts, lights) on secondary roads ≤55 mph, no interstates. Before then "Off Road Use Only" vehicles cannot be registered (§ 56-1-10(37)) and unregistered vehicles are barred from highways (§ 56-3-110). Chandler's Law (§ 50-26-20) defines ATV by handlebars, so steering-wheel UTVs are outside it.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Georgia (O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120) and South Carolina (S.C. Code § 56-15-10) restrict side-by-side operation on public roads, with limited exceptions.
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia does not generally allow it; South Carolina allows only registered UTVs on certain roads, starting Nov. 18, 2026 (S.C. Act 164 of 2026).

cites.cite: 2026 S.C. Act No. 164 (S. 222), adding S.C. Code §§ 56-2-5000 et seq., eff. Nov. 18, 2026

replacements.note: PRIMARY. Keep "Generally no." for now; revisit after 11/18/2026 when SC answer changes for registered UTVs.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Georgia's ATV statute (O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120 et seq.) establishes age-based restrictions for ATV operation.
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia's Off-Road Vehicle Act (O.C.G.A. § 40-7-1 et seq.) sets no minimum age for ATV operators.
replacements.note: PRIMARY. Verified: Chapter 7 (2025 Code) has six sections and none addresses age.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Children under 16 are prohibited from operating an ATV on public land unless they have completed an approved ATV safety course.
replacements.new_sentence: The one statutory age rule is narrow: a farmer must be 16 or older to drive an ATV on a public road (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-305).
replacements.note: ADJACENT unsupported (it is South Carolina's rule, not Georgia's). "One statutory age rule" refers to Title 40; if unsure about DNR property rules, soften to "Georgia's main statutory age rule".

replacements.old_sentence_exact: The law also restricts children from operating ATVs with engine sizes that exceed age-appropriate limits established by the CPSC.
replacements.new_sentence: Youth size limits come from manufacturer age-warning labels and CPSC guidance, not Georgia statute.
replacements.note: ADJACENT unsupported: no Georgia engine-size statute.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Parents and guardians who knowingly permit a child to violate these restrictions may face both criminal penalties and civil liability.
replacements.note: ADJACENT unsupported for Georgia: Chapter 7 violations are expressly not criminal (§ 40-7-6, civil penalty). South Carolina does criminalize parental violations (§ 50-26-30, § 50-26-60 misdemeanor). Recommend deleting; the SC sentence below covers SC.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: South Carolina's off-highway vehicle statute (S.C. Code § 56-15-10 et seq.) similarly restricts minor ATV operation and requires parental supervision.
replacements.new_sentence: South Carolina law (S.C. Code § 50-26-10 et seq.) bars ATV use under age 6 and requires a helmet and safety course through age 15.
replacements.note: § 50-26-30(A) (parent may not let under-6 operate), (F) hands-on course certificate for 15 and younger, (G) FMVSS 218 helmet + eye protection; § 50-26-40(C) adult accompaniment for 16 and younger on lands open to the public; § 50-26-60 misdemeanor $50–$200. Exceptions § 50-26-70: farm/ranch, hunting/trapping, and ages 6–15 on private property under direct parental visual supervision.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Georgia law (O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120) restricts children under 16 from operating ATVs on public land without a safety course and prohibits age-inappropriate engine sizes.
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia's Off-Road Vehicle Act (O.C.G.A. § 40-7-1 et seq.) sets no minimum operator age; South Carolina bars ATV operation under age 6 (S.C. Code § 50-26-30).
replacements.note: PRIMARY. The FAQ's first sentence ("CPSC recommends no ATV use for children under 6") was not verified in this pass.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Commercial ATV operations must also comply with O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120 (Georgia) and S.C. Code § 56-15-10 (South Carolina) governing off-highway vehicle operation.
replacements.new_sentence: Commercial ATV operations must also comply with Georgia's off-road vehicle law (O.C.G.A. § 40-7-1 et seq.) and South Carolina's ATV law (S.C. Code § 50-26-10 et seq.).
replacements.note: PRIMARY. Chandler's Law applies to riders including tour customers (under-16 certificate, helmets, adult accompaniment on public lands).

replacements.old_sentence_exact: Georgia law under O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120 et seq. generally prohibits operating ATVs on public roads, with exceptions for agricultural purposes, road crossings, and certain designated areas.
replacements.new_sentence: Georgia law does not generally allow ATVs on public roads; O.C.G.A. § 40-6-305 lets farmers 16 and older use them for farm hauling, and O.C.G.A. § 40-7-5 lets localities set zones of use.
replacements.note: PRIMARY. "Road crossings" exception has no Georgia statutory basis — dropped. § 40-7-5 authorizes local ordinances on "time periods and zones of use" (not necessarily roads). URL is the chapter page (lists § 40-7-5).

replacements.old_sentence_exact: When an ATV is legally crossing or traveling along a roadway under these exceptions, the operator must comply with applicable traffic laws and safety equipment requirements.
replacements.new_sentence: A farmer lawfully driving an ATV on a road has the same duties as any other driver (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-306) and must display a slow-moving-vehicle emblem.
replacements.note: ADJACENT: drops the crossing premise. § 40-6-306 text read from the public-domain OCGA mirror (2021 release); § 40-6-305(b)(1) emblem requirement verified on Justia 2025. Left unlinked: the Part 1B page was not opened in a browser.

replacements.old_sentence_exact: South Carolina's off-highway vehicle statute (S.C. Code § 56-15-10 et seq.) similarly restricts ATV road use, though specific regulations vary by county and municipality.
